'''Cédric Patrice Thierry Villani''' ({{IPA|fr|sedʁik patʁis tjeʁi vilani|lang}}; born 5 October 1973) is a French [[List of mathematician-politicians|mathematician and politician]] working primarily on [[partial differential equation]]s, [[Riemannian geometry]] and [[mathematical physics]]. He was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 2010, and he was the director of [[Sorbonne University]]'s [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] from 2009 to 2017. As of September 2025, he is a professor at the [[École normale supérieure de Rennes]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=La star des mathématiques Cédric Villani a fait sa rentrée à l'Université de Rennes |url=https://etudiant.lefigaro.fr/article/etudes/la-star-des-mathematiques-cedric-villani-a-fait-sa-rentree-a-l-universite-de-rennes-20250905/ |last=Mercier |first=Romain |date=2025-09-05 |website=[[Le Figaro]] étudiant}}</ref>

Villani has given two lectures at the [[Royal Institution]], the first titled 'Birth of a Theorem'.<ref>{{cite web |title=Birth of a Theorem |first=Cédric |last=Villani |date=22 April 2015 |publisher=The Royal Institution |via=YouTube |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yYwydG_aHPE&list=PLbnrZHfNEDZyDfeVsNBMNDUu-o5j9_QMb&index=12  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/yYwydG_aHPE |archive-date=15 December 2021 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The English translation of his book ''Théorème vivant'' (''Living Theorem'') has the same title. 
In the book he describes the links between his research on [[kinetic theory of gases|kinetic theory]] and that of the mathematician [[Carlo Cercignani]]. Villani, in fact, proved the so-called [[Cercignani conjecture|Cercignani's conjecture]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}} His second lecture at the Royal Institution is titled 'The Extraordinary Theorems of [[John Forbes Nash Jr.|John Nash]]'.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Extraordinary Theorems of John Nash |first=Cédric |last=Villani |date=2 November 2016 |publisher=The Royal Institution |via=YouTube |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iHKa8F-RsEM&list=PLbnrZHfNEDZyDfeVsNBMNDUu-o5j9_QMb&index=9  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/iHKa8F-RsEM |archive-date=15 December 2021 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Villani was elected as the deputy for [[Essonne's 5th constituency]] in the [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]], the lower house of the [[French Parliament]], during the [[2017 French legislative election|2017 legislative election]].<ref name="2017-05-12_ABC">[http://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-05-12/macron-team-announces-candidates-for-france-parliament-election/8519826 Emmanuel Macron team announces candidates for France's June parliamentary election], [[ABC News Online]], 12 May 2017.</ref>  He was elected as a member of [[La République En Marche!]] (LREM), but in May 2020 left the party to form a new party, [[Ecology, Democracy, Solidarity]] (EDS).<ref>{{Cite news|date=19 May 2020|title=Macron loses majority as defectors form new party|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-52721153|access-date=20 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thelocal.fr/20200519/macrons-party-loses-majority-in-the-french-parliament|website=www.thelocal.fr|access-date=20 May 2020|title=Macron's party loses outright majority in French parliament|date=19 May 2020}}</ref> Following the dissolution of EDS, Villani joined [[Ecology Generation]], and ran for re-election [[2022 French legislative election|in 2022]] under the banner of the [[NUPES]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.liberation.fr/politique/aux-ulis-cedric-villani-defend-sa-nouvelle-etiquette-nupes-20220523_GS2ICXG3RNHBVBCBPPPFMYYIOM/|title=Legislative: in Ulis, Cédric Villani defends his new label Nupes|website=Liberation|last1=Derestiat|first1=Anthony|date=23 May 2022|accessdate=6 June 2022}}</ref> ultimately [[List of MPs who lost their seat in the 2022 French legislative election|losing his seat]] to LREM candidate [[Paul Midy]] by 19 votes.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Ministère de l'Intérieur|title=Résultats des élections législatives 2022 |url=http://www.interieur.gouv.fr/Elections/Les-resultats/Legislatives/elecresult__legislatives-2022 |access-date=24 September 2022 |website=[[French Government]] |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

He was elected vice president of the French [[Parliamentary Office for the Evaluation of Scientific and Technological Choices]] in July 2017.

==Biography==
After attending the [[Lycée Louis-le-Grand]], Villani was admitted at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris and studied there from 1992 to 1996, after which he was appointed an [[agrégé préparateur]] at the same school.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cedricvillani.org/biography/|last=Villani|first=Cédric|title=Biography|access-date=11 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190411063837/https://cedricvillani.org/biography/|archive-date=11 April 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> He received his doctorate at [[Paris Dauphine University]] in 1998, under the supervision of [[Pierre-Louis Lions]], and became professor at the [[École normale supérieure de Lyon]] in 2000. He is now professor at the [[University of Lyon]]. He was director of the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]] in Paris from 2009 to 2017.<ref>[http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=56307 Mathematics Genealogy Project – Cédric Villani]. Accessed on line 20 August 2010.</ref><ref name=fm>{{cite web |url=http://www.icm2010.in/prize-winners-2010/fields-medal-cedric-villani |title=Fields Medal – Cédric Villani |access-date=20 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100829111903/http://www.icm2010.in/prize-winners-2010/fields-medal-cedric-villani |archive-date=29 August 2010}}</ref>

He has held various visiting positions at [[Georgia Tech]] (Fall 1999), the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (Spring 2004), and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]] (Spring 2009).<ref>{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae (Cédric Villani)|url=http://cedricvillani.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/cv-2012.pdf|website=cedricvillani.org|access-date=24 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160623224603/http://cedricvillani.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/cv-2012.pdf|archive-date=23 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Mathematical work==
Villani has worked on the theory of [[partial differential equations]] involved in [[statistical mechanics]], specifically the [[Boltzmann equation]], where, with Laurent Desvillettes, he was the first to prove how quickly convergence occurs for initial values not near equilibrium.<ref name=fm /> He has written with Giuseppe Toscani on this subject. With [[Clément Mouhot]], he has worked on nonlinear [[Landau damping]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Clément Mouhot |author2=Cédric Villani |title=Landau damping |doi=10.1063/1.3285283 |year=2010 |journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics |volume=51 |pages=015204 |issue=15204 |arxiv=0905.2167|bibcode=2010JMP....51a5204M |s2cid=14883238 }}</ref> He has worked on the theory of [[optimal transport]] and its applications to differential geometry, and with [[John Lott (mathematician)|John Lott]] has defined a notion of bounded [[Ricci curvature]] for general measured length spaces.<ref>{{cite arXiv |eprint=math/0412127 |author1=John Lott |author2=Cedric Villani |title=Ricci curvature for metric-measure spaces via optimal transport |year=2004 }}</ref> He also served on the Mathematical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] in 2015 and 2016.

Villani received the Fields Medal for his work on [[Landau damping]] and the [[Boltzmann equation]].<ref name=fm /> He described the development of his theorem in his autobiographical book ''Théorème vivant'' (2012), published in [[English language|English translation]] as ''Birth of a Theorem: A Mathematical Adventure'' (2015).<ref>{{cite web| author=Ashbacher, Charles|date=7 May 2015|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/birth-of-a-theorem|title=Review of ''Birth of a Theorem'' by Cédric Villani|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Alexander, Amir|author-link=Amir Alexander|title=Mathematics: Groping in the dark for glimpses of beauty (joint review of ''Birth of a Theorem'' by Cédric Villani and ''Mathematics without Apologies'' by Michael Harris)|journal=Nature|volume=519|issue=7541|pages=31–32|date=4 March 2015|doi=10.1038/519031a|doi-access=free}} (See [[Michael Harris (mathematician)|Michael Harris]].)</ref> He gave a [[TED (conference)|TED talk]] at the 2016 conference in Vancouver.<ref name="TED">{{cite web|title=Cédric Villani: What's so sexy about math?|date=6 June 2016 |url=https://www.ted.com/talks/cedric_villani_what_s_so_sexy_about_math|publisher=[[TED (conference)|TED]]|access-date=8 June 2016}}</ref>

== Political career ==
[[File:Réunion publique de La République En Marche ! Japon, avec le député Cédric Villani le jeudi 26 novembre de à Akasaka, Tokyo.jpg|thumb|Cédric Villani at a public meeting of En Marche in Tokyo]]
In 2017, it was announced that Villani had been selected as a candidate for ''[[La République En Marche!|En Marche!]]'' (LREM) in the [[2017 French legislative election]], for [[Essonne's 5th constituency]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-39881266|title=France's Macron announces gender equal list of political outsiders|date=11 May 2017|work=BBC News|access-date=11 May 2017|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en-marche.fr/article/communique-liste-investis|title=Communiqué de presse – Liste des investis aux élections législatives {{!}} En Marche !|website=En Marche !|access-date=11 May 2017}}</ref> In the first round of voting, Villani obtained 47% of the vote and was thus strongly placed for the second round<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liberation.fr/elections-presidentielle-legislatives-2017/2017/06/15/cedric-villani-l-idee-c-est-d-avoir-des-competences-variees_1577148|title=Cédric Villani : "L'idée, c'est d'avoir des compétences variées"|website=Libération|date=15 June 2017|access-date=18 June 2017|archive-date=17 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170617073544/http://www.liberation.fr/elections-presidentielle-legislatives-2017/2017/06/15/cedric-villani-l-idee-c-est-d-avoir-des-competences-variees_1577148|url-status=dead}}</ref> which he won with 69.36% of the vote.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://elections.interieur.gouv.fr/legislatives-2017/091/09105.html|title=Elections législatives 2017|author=Ministère de l'Intérieur|website=elections.interieur.gouv.fr|access-date=19 June 2017}}</ref>

In 2019, Villani applied to be selected to lead the LREM candidate slate for [[2020 French municipal elections|the 2020 Paris election]]. By July 2019, he was one of three LREM candidates, all [[List of deputies of the 15th National Assembly of France|deputies in the]] [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]], still seeking the position; the other two were [[Benjamin Griveaux]] (who had been the [[List of Government spokespeople of France|government spokesperson]]) and [[Hugues Renson]] (who had been the vice-president of the National Assembly). On 10 July, the nomination committee picked Griveaux.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/politique/article/2019/07/10/elections-municipales-a-paris-villani-annonce-qu-il-ne-sera-pas-investi-par-la-republique-en-marche_5487851_823448.html|title=Elections municipales à Paris: Benjamin Griveaux choisi pour représenter LRM|last=Cosnard|first=Denis|date=10 July 2019|work=[[Le Monde]]|access-date=3 August 2019|language=fr}}</ref> On 4 September, Villani officially announced his candidacy for the municipal election.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/politique/municipales-cedric-villani-officialise-sa-candidature-a-la-mairie-de-paris-04-09-2019-8145645.php|title=Municipales : Cédric Villani officialise sa candidature à la mairie de Paris|author=R. Bx.|date=4 September 2019|website=leparisien.fr|language=fr-FR|access-date=5 September 2019}}</ref>

==Other activities==
* France China Foundation, former Member of the Strategic Committee<ref>{{cite web
|url=https://francechinafoundation.org/strategic/ 
|title=France China Foundation Strategic Committee
|archive-date=10 June 2017
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170610024441/http://francechinafoundation.org/strategic/}}
</ref>
In 2018, the [[France|French]] [[economics]] [[magazine]] [[Challenges (magazine)|Challenges]] said that Villani has been approached by Europanova [[thinktank]]. He presided over the jury of Digital In-Pulse, a startup program dedicated to accompanying entrepreneurs and start-ups, managed by [[China|Chinese]] [[corporate]] [[Huawei]]. The magazine also says that Villani is still the President of the endowment funds of the French [[Institut Henri Poincaré|Henri Poincaré Institute]], and [[Huawei]] is among the top private donors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Izambard |first=Antoine |date=2018-06-27 |title=Comment la France surveille le géant des télécoms Huawei |url=https://www.challenges.fr/entreprise/telecoms/comment-la-france-surveille-de-tres-pres-le-geant-chinois-des-telecoms-huawei_596680 |access-date=2025-03-01 |website=Challenges |language=fr}}</ref> Villani declined the journalist's request for comment, and the article indicates that the French [[counter-intelligence]] service presented him as "too naïve" regarding those opportunities.

==Awards and honours==

===Diplomas, titles and awards===
* 1998: PhD Thesis (advisor P.-L. Lions)
* 2000: Habilitation dissertation
* 2001: Louis Armand Prize of the Academy of Sciences
* 2003: Peccot-Vimont Prize and Cours Peccot of the Collège de France
* 2003: Plenary lecturer at the International Congress of Mathematical Physics (Lisbonne)
* 2004: Harold Grad lecturer
* 2004: Visiting [[Miller Institute|Miller]] Professor, University of California Berkeley. 
* 2006: Institut Universitaire de France
* 2006: Invited lecturer at the International Congress of Mathematicians (Madrid)<ref>{{cite book|chapter=''Hypocoercive diffusion operators'' by Cédric Villani|editor=Sanz-Solé, M.|editor2=Soria, J.|editor3=Varona, J. L.|editor4=Verdera, J.|year=2007|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians Madrid, August 22–30, 2006|publisher=European Mathematical Society|pages=473–498|volume=III|isbn=978-3-03719-022-7|chapter-url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM2006.3/ICM2006.3.ocr.pdf}}</ref>
* 2007: {{ill|Grand Prix Jacques Herbrand|fr}} ([[French Academy of Sciences#Medals, awards and prizes|French Academy of Sciences]])
* 2008: Prize of the [[European Mathematical Society]]
* 2009: [[Henri Poincaré Prize]]
* 2009: [[Fermat Prize]]
* 2010: [[Fields Medal]]
* 2013: [[Josiah Willard Gibbs Lectureship|Gibbs lecturer]]: ''On Disorder, Mixing and Equilibration''<ref>[https://www.ams.org/meetings/lectures/meet-gibbs-lect Josiah Willard Gibbs Lectures – No. 86, January 2013, San Diego, CA; Cédric Villani] Accessed on line 20 May 2015.</ref>
* 2014: [[Joseph L. Doob Prize]] by the [[American Mathematical Society]] for his book ''Optimal Transport: Old and New'' (Springer Verlag 2009)<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/ams-prizes/doob-prize Joseph L. Doob Prize – Most Recent Prize: 2014] Accessed on line 20 May 2015.</ref>

===Extra-academic distinctions===
* 2009: Knight of the [[National Order of Merit (France)]]
* 2011: Knight of the [[Legion of Honor]]
* 2013: Member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]<ref>[http://www.upmc.fr/en/research/talents_and_discoveries/scientific_awards_and_honors/2013/cedric_villani_elected_to_the_academy_of_science.html Cédric Villani, new member of the French Academy of Science] Accessed on line 20 May 2015.</ref>
* 2016: Ordinary member of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]]
* 2022: Fellow of the [[International Science Council]]

In 2020, a supposed new spider species of the family [[Araneidae]], ''Araniella villanii'', was named after him. However, this species was later shown to be a junior synonym of ''[[Araniella tbilisiensis]]''.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://wsc.nmbe.ch/spec-data/9923 | title= ''Araniella'' ''tbilisiensis'' (Mcheidze, 1997)| website=[[World Spider Catalog]] | date=17 April 2026 }}</ref>
